structure.heading: 2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Capacity Assumptions
text_content: **2026 Headcount Forecast by Function and Capacity Assumptions**

By plan year-end the organization increases total headcount from 1,200 on 2025-12-31 to 1,320 on 2026-12-31, a net addition of +120 headcount representing a 10.0% increase. This growth aligns with strategic priorities for product expansion and market penetration scheduled across 2026. The headcount target presumes execution across twelve months, with quarterly checkpoint reviews on 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30, and 2026-09-30 to validate hiring pace, budget variance, and operational capacity against the 2026-12-31 objective. Finance will publish monthly hiring dashboards to enable tracking.

Function-level allocations reflect concentrated investment in Engineering and Sales. Engineering headcount increases from 420 on 2025-12-31 to 500 on 2026-12-31, a +80 change (+19.05%), supporting accelerated product delivery and platform scalability. Sales grows from 260 on 2025-12-31 to 290 on 2026-12-31, a +30 change (+11.54%), enabling expanded go-to-market coverage. The remaining +10 headcount (to reach total +120) is allocated to Customer Success, Data, and Operations to sustain retention, analytics, and operating cadence. Engineering staffing focuses on backend, infrastructure, and security.

Our capacity model assumes an annual voluntary attrition rate of 12.0% applied to the 2025 baseline, with role-specific time-to-fill assumptions: Engineering 70 days and Sales 45 days median. Offer acceptance is modeled at 80% with a 1.25:1 offer-to-req ratio. New hire productivity ramps linearly to full capacity at six months for Engineering and three months for Sales, delivering approximately 60% and 80% of steady-state output in month one respectively. Budget assumes average fully-burdened cost per FTE of $140,000 in 2026.

The hiring cadence is phased monthly to meet the 2026-12-31 target with prioritized fills in Q1 and Q2 for critical Engineering cores and Q3 expansion for Sales. A contingency buffer of 10% overplan in requisitions accounts for attrition and offer fallout. Scenario sensitivity modeled: base +120, downside -15% hiring pace, upside +10% acceleration. Key monitoring metrics include hires-to-plan, time-to-productivity, budget variance, and headcount by function reviewed weekly by People Operations and Finance. Monthly dashboards will drive corrective actions and approvals.

structure.heading: Critical Skill Gaps and Internal Mobility vs. External Hiring Talent Acquisition Plan
text_content: **Critical Skill Gaps and Internal Mobility vs. External Hiring Talent Acquisition Plan**

The 2026 critical skill gaps identified in this forecast require immediate attention: 35 Data Engineers, 20 Cloud Security Engineers, and 15 Product Managers. These shortfalls concentrate risk within Data & Analytics, Cloud Infrastructure, and Product organizations, threatening roadmap delivery for Q1–Q4 2026 and key initiatives with projected revenue impact in FY2026. HR Business Partners and Engineering leadership must treat these as priority hires and internal development targets; otherwise projected capacity constraints will increase time-to-market and escalate contractor spend. The profile of required competencies includes scalable ETL design, cloud-native security tooling (IAM, WAF, CSPM), and product discovery expertise with stakeholder facilitation at senior levels.

Our recommended fill mix balances growth and retention: 60% internal mobility (72 of 120 roles) and 40% external hiring (48 of 120 roles). By setting an internal mobility target of 72 positions, People & Culture and Learning & Development will deploy accelerated reskilling programs, rotational assignments, and defined succession plans across the affected functions beginning Q2 2025 and scaling through 2026. Expected benefits include reduced hiring cost-per-hire, faster cultural assimilation, and improved institutional knowledge transfer; risks include uneven geographic capability and temporary backfill reqs.. Governance will include quarterly talent reviews, competency assessments, and targeted career pathways for Data, Cloud, and Product streams.

The external hiring plan will address the remaining 48 roles with an operational target: an average time-to-fill of 55 days in 2026. Talent Acquisition (TA) will prioritize roles by criticality—Cloud Security Engineers and Data Engineers receive top sourcing focus—using a mix of direct sourcing, university partnerships, specialist agencies, and diversity-focused job boards and referrals. Key execution steps include: 1. streamlined interview templates and calibrated scorecards; 2. dedicated TA pod per function; 3. competitive compensation benchmarking with quarterly adjustments. Monitoring will be weekly via a TA dashboard, with escalation to HR leadership if average time-to-fill exceeds 70 days or offer-acceptance falls below 70%.
